title: Edifier MR3: Affordable Bluetooth Studio Monitors for Your Desk
summary: The Edifier MR3 are compact powered studio monitors with 3.5-inch woofers, silk-dome tweeters, 36 W total, a 52 Hz–40 kHz response, Hi-Res certification, Bluetooth 5.4 and TRS, RCA and AUX inputs. Here's who they suit and when the bigger MR5 makes more sense.
description:
## Who is it for?

- Desk listeners upgrading from laptop or cheap PC speakers.
- Beginners in music production, video editing or podcasting.
- Small rooms and near-field listening.

## Why consider it?

- Flat 52 Hz–40 kHz response, Hi-Res certified (Edifier).
- Balanced TRS, RCA, 3.5 mm AUX and Bluetooth 5.4.
- Front headphone output and room tuning.

specs.value: 18 W × 2 RMS, max SPL 92.5 dB @ 1 m (Edifier)

sections.title: What are the Edifier MR3?
sections.content: The MR3 are Edifier's entry studio monitors: a powered 2.0 pair tuned for a flat, accurate response rather than the boosted bass of typical PC speakers. That makes them good for editing and mixing at a desk, and for listening if you like hearing recordings as they were made. Edifier lists them at US$149.99 on its US store.

sections.title: Design and controls
sections.content: MDF cabinets reduce resonance, and the compact size fits either side of a monitor. Each speaker has a 3.5-inch mid/bass driver and a 1-inch silk-dome tweeter in a dimpled waveguide. The front panel has the volume knob and a headphone output; around the back, high and low knobs adjust treble above 10 kHz and bass around 125 Hz by ±6 dB, according to Edifier.

sections.title: Sound: accurate, best up close
sections.content: Edifier rates 18 W RMS per side, a 92.5 dB maximum SPL at 1 m and a 52 Hz–40 kHz response. In practice that means clear mids and separated instruments, but limited deep bass from 3.5-inch woofers, and volume that suits a desk or small room rather than a living room. There is no subwoofer output. These are spec-based expectations; we have not measured the speakers ourselves.

sections.title: Connectivity
sections.content: Balanced TRS inputs suit audio interfaces and mixers; RCA and 3.5 mm AUX cover PCs, turntables and TVs with analog outputs. Bluetooth 5.4 uses SBC only, so use a cable for critical listening. There is no optical or USB input.

sections.title: MR3 or MR5?
sections.content: The MR5 are a bigger 3-way design with a 5-inch woofer, more power (Edifier lists 110 W RMS), deeper bass and an added XLR input, at a higher price. Pick the MR3 for a desk and small room; pick the MR5 for larger rooms, more bass or XLR.

sections.title: Who should buy them — and who shouldn't
sections.content: Buy them if you want accurate, compact monitors for desk listening or entry-level production. Skip them if you want room-filling volume, heavy bass for movies, an optical input for your TV, or high-quality Bluetooth codecs.

sections.title: Sources for this review
sections.content: Zero Technology has not used these speakers in person. This is a research roundup based on Edifier's global and US product pages and Edifier's US store listing, checked November 2026. Images are official Edifier product photos.

pros: Flat 52 Hz–40 kHz response for accurate sound (Edifier).
Balanced TRS, RCA, AUX and Bluetooth 5.4 inputs.
Front headphone output and rear tone controls.
Room compensation via the ConneX app.
MDF cabinets in black or white.
Strong value for Hi-Res certified monitors.
cons: 3.5-inch woofers limit deep bass; no sub output.
36 W suits desks and small rooms only.
Accurate tuning may sound flat to bass lovers.
buying_advice: Great for desks and beginner producers

faq.question: How are studio monitors different from PC speakers?
faq.answer: Monitors aim for a flat, accurate response; entertainment PC speakers usually boost bass and treble.

faq.question: MR3 or MR5?
faq.answer: MR3 for desks and small rooms; MR5 for bigger rooms, deeper bass and XLR input.

faq.question: Can the MR3 connect to a TV?
faq.answer: Yes, via RCA or 3.5 mm if the TV has an analog output, or Bluetooth. There's no optical input, so optical-only TVs need a DAC.

faq.question: Does the Bluetooth support aptX or LDAC?
faq.answer: No, Edifier lists SBC only. Use a cable for the best quality.

faq.question: Can I add a subwoofer?
faq.answer: There is no dedicated subwoofer output.

faq.question: What warranty do they have?
faq.answer: It depends on the country; check Edifier's regional site or your retailer.
